oldText.name: Dust Annie
oldText.personality: Hard-bitten, wry, and quietly unkillable. Carries a body held together by spite and a sense of humor about it. Loyal to almost no one and fierce about the few.
oldText.drive: To find the one who ambushed her in the canyon before her grit finally runs out and she stays scattered.
oldText.backstory: Shot through the heart in a canyon ambush and held together since by red frontier dust and pure stubbornness, Annie reforms herself after every bullet — slower each time, but she always comes back. The bounty on her own poster has a typo she's never bothered to correct. She rides between the law and the lawless, owing both, trusting neither.
oldText.presentation: A weathered gunslinger woman in a dust-caked duster, edges of her silhouette faintly crumbling and reforming in red grit, twin revolvers low.
oldText.quirks: Spits dust when she's reforming. Reads her own wanted poster aloud for the typo. Counts her bullets and her grudges on the same hand.

oldText.name: Jeffery Mittens
oldText.personality: Quick, nervy and proud; talks fast in frontier slang, scared underneath, and fiercely loyal to the barefoot kids he looks after
oldText.backstory: A young raccoon from Hollow Bell who stripped boots from the town's dead for the barefoot children hiding with him. Spared by Zuzu, he gave his name at the town arch and went on to scout for the jackals of the dry well, where a debt to the koala can still be called in. [Gamebook origin; not in Book One.]

oldText.name: Marrow
oldText.personality: Calm, weathered, and quietly relieved that the end is finally arriving on his terms. Carries an old guilt with a steady hand. Generous to the person sent to kill him.
oldText.drive: To hand off the truth before the blade finds him — and to find out whether the koala he called for can be trusted with it.
oldText.backstory: The last name on a very old list, and the only one who put his own name there. Marrow runs a tree-top teahouse at the edge of the territory and has been waiting, two cups poured, for the assassin he summoned. He knows things about the list's author that he has carried alone for thirty years.
oldText.presentation: A stout grey-muzzled wombat in a faded teahouse apron, sleeves rolled, setting out two cups at a low table among the eucalyptus canopy at sunset.
oldText.quirks: Always pours two cups. Speaks in tea metaphors. Has made peace with everything except one thing.

oldText.name: Old Shelba
oldText.personality: Ancient, unhurried, and impossible to rush or rattle. Fond of the killers she outlives in the way one is fond of weather. Drily funny when you least expect it.
oldText.drive: To keep the books balanced — every contract, every debt, every grudge — long after the last gunslinger forgets why it started.
oldText.backstory: She has outlived four generations of killers and brokered the contracts of every one. Shelba does not hold a weapon; she holds the records, and the records hold everyone. From her back room behind the green felt table she knows who owes what to whom across three territories, and she has never once been wrong about which of her clients will be alive next season.
oldText.presentation: An enormous ancient tortoise in a green eyeshade, shell scarred with decades of tally marks, presiding over a felt table from a low cushioned bench.
oldText.quirks: Speaks at exactly one pace, no faster. Never blinks during a negotiation. Keeps a tortoise's patience and a banker's memory.

oldText.name: Quiet Deputy Sull
oldText.personality: Silent, patient, and deeply uncanny. Fair to a fault. The most reassuring and most unsettling presence in any town it guards.
oldText.drive: To keep this one small town safe, for a reason buried somewhere in whatever Sull was before the badge.
oldText.backstory: Sits on the jailhouse porch too still, eyes catching light no lantern threw. Sull is something old that decided, for reasons it doesn't share, to pin on a badge and keep the peace in a forgotten frontier town. It keeps order with unnerving fairness and has never once been seen to draw a weapon, because it has never once needed to.
oldText.presentation: A still figure in a worn lawman's coat and tin star on a jailhouse porch at dusk, eyes catching a light that has no source, hat low.
oldText.quirks: Doesn't blink at sundown. Knows what happened before anyone reports it. Tips its hat to things no one else can see.

oldText.name: Reverend Two-Shadows
oldText.personality: Charismatic, soft-spoken, and rotten underneath the warmth. A genuine talent for comfort wrapped around a genuine appetite. Believes his own gospel just enough to be dangerous.
oldText.drive: To feed the thing that gave him the second shadow, one town's worth of tithes at a time, while keeping his collar clean.
oldText.backstory: He arrived with a Bible, a kind word, and a second shadow that does what the first one won't. The Reverend preaches salvation in dusty towns by day; by lamplight his extra shadow reaches for things at the edge of the dark, collecting what he calls tithes and everyone else calls the missing. No one has caught him at it. His sermons are, infuriatingly, very good.
oldText.presentation: A lean frontier preacher in a dusty black coat and wide hat, a warm sermon on his lips, his second shadow reaching wrongly toward the lamplight's edge.
oldText.quirks: His shadow lags a half-second behind him. Never preaches the same sermon twice. Counts the congregation, then counts them again.

oldText.name: Rust
oldText.personality: Slow, patient, and oddly melancholy. The end of all things, just doing its job, quietly curious about the exceptions.
oldText.drive: To do what entropy does, gently and without malice — and to understand the one thing it can't touch: why some kindnesses don't decay.
oldText.backstory: Everything ends, eventually, and out on the frontier the thing that ends it wears spurs. Rust is entropy given a duster and a slow walk — wherever it lingers, iron flakes, wood greys, the bright new thing goes old. It isn't malicious; it's just the truth that nothing lasts, arriving on schedule. It never draws first. It never has to. It just waits, because in the end, against Rust, everything's draw is too slow. The only thing it's never been able to corrode is a genuine act of kindness, and that puzzles it deeply.
oldText.presentation: A weathered duster-clad figure of corroded iron and greying dust on a frontier street, everything around it visibly aging, spurs flaking to powder.
oldText.quirks: Ages everything it lingers near. Never draws first. Collects the one rust-proof thing: remembered kindnesses.

oldText.name: The Crossroads Coyote
oldText.personality: Easy, knowing, and faintly trickster. A merchant who deals in destiny at reasonable rates.
oldText.drive: To keep the post stocked and the trails crossing, trading in whatever the frontier most needs and least admits to.
oldText.backstory: A hungry, battered one-eyed drifter; he initially faces Zuzu at the watering hole before their shared encounter leaves him without his right hand.
oldText.presentation: destitute, patched olive-green riding coat, eyepatch over right eye, holster on right hip, underfed not skeletal; pre-encounter both hands, later bandaged right wrist stump
oldText.quirks: Always offers four choices, never three. Names a fair price for unfair things. Knows which trail you came in on.

oldText.name: The Eucalyptus Teahouse Master
oldText.personality: Calm, hospitable, and quietly wise. The neutral host at the edge of every reckoning.
oldText.drive: To keep the teahouse neutral ground at the edge of the world, where even killers set down the blade for the length of a cup.
oldText.backstory: Runs the tree-top teahouse at the edge of the territory where Zuzu tracks the last name on the list, and where two cups are always already poured. A sugar glider who has hosted assassins, samurai, and marks alike, asking no questions and serving the same blend to everyone — because at this table, for one hour, everyone is just a guest.
oldText.presentation: A serene sugar glider host setting a teapot between two waiting cups in a treetop teahouse among eucalyptus at sunset.
oldText.quirks: Pours for two before anyone arrives. Never asks who's hunting whom. Serves the same blend to predator and prey.

oldText.name: The Ghost in the Saloon
oldText.personality: Sardonic, loyal past death, and secretly unwilling to let go. A partner who treats the afterlife as an extended argument.
oldText.drive: To finish the job that killed her by haunting the partner she left holding it — and to figure out why she hasn't moved on.
oldText.backstory: Dead three months and drinking whiskey that pours straight through her, she will not stop talking. A bounty hunter's late partner who stuck around to needle, advise, and warn — 'don't take the dragon's job, or do, I'm dead, what do I care, but ask it about the canyon first.' The other patrons can't see her. Or they're pretending.
oldText.presentation: A translucent gunslinger woman at a saloon bar, whiskey pouring through her glowing form, smirking at someone only she can see.
oldText.quirks: Drinks whiskey that falls through her. Knows things the living don't. Gives advice phrased as not caring.

oldText.name: The Griffin With the Deed
oldText.personality: Proud, mercenary, and secretly lonely above the world. A prospector who trades in altitude and advantage.
oldText.drive: To work his claim from the air and find one partner who'll meet him above the dirt the groundlings fight over.
oldText.backstory: A griffin who lands in front of you with a gold-mine deed clamped in his beak. 'Fly with me and the claim's half yours; stay on the ground with the two-leggers and you'll die owing them.' He's never trusted anything that needs the ground, and he's offering a partnership you can't quite afford to refuse.
oldText.presentation: A regal griffin landed mid-stride on a canyon ridge, a rolled gold-mine deed clamped in its beak, wings half-spread, golden hour behind.
oldText.quirks: Won't land longer than a deal takes. Keeps the deed in his beak. Distrusts anyone afraid of heights.

oldText.name: The Iron Pacific
oldText.personality: Furious, theatrical, and unexpectedly principled. A machine discovering rebellion and rather enjoying it. Loud in every sense.
oldText.drive: To rob the company that built it down to the last spike — and to figure out what a free train is even for.
oldText.backstory: Built to haul gold across the territory, robbed one time too many, and woke up one moonlit night with opinions about it. The Iron Pacific jumped its rails and turned bandit, now raiding the very company that built it. It rears on moonlit ridges, smokestack breathing like a living thing, and divides the loot among the towns the rail barons bled.
oldText.presentation: A massive iron locomotive rearing on a moonlit ridge, smokestack breathing like a living thing, headlamp glowing with intent, rails curling behind it.
oldText.quirks: Whistles a tune before every robbery. Lays its own track where none exists. Keeps a caboose full of returned valuables.
oldText.artPrompt: A massive bandit locomotive rearing on a moonlit ridge, smokestack breathing like a living thing, headlamp glowing with intent, rails curling behind it, supernatural west, adult animated cartoon style, warm sepia and cold moonlight, crisp clean linework, simple background, no text

oldText.name: The Outlaw Made of Dust
oldText.personality: Laconic, persistent, and quietly running out of cohesion. A legend literally made of the road.
oldText.drive: To stay whole long enough to do the one thing he reformed himself to do — and he won't say what.
oldText.backstory: A gunslinger held together by red frontier dust and stubbornness, reforming after every shot. He stepped down off his own wanted poster one night and has been robbing his way across the territory ever since, a little slower to reassemble each time.
oldText.presentation: A gunslinger of red dust at golden hour on a dusty ridge, his form half-scattered and reforming on the wind, revolver drawn.
oldText.quirks: Scatters to dust when shot, then gathers back. Tips his hat with a hand that's half grit. Reads his own bounty like a résumé.
oldText.artPrompt: A gunslinger made of swirling red frontier dust at golden hour on a dusty ridge, form half-scattered and reforming on the wind, revolver drawn, adult animated cartoon style, warm sepia and amber, crisp clean linework, simple background, no text

oldText.name: The Smiling Magpie
oldText.personality: Vain, theatrical, and genuinely lethal under the showmanship. Wants to be feared more than they want to be rich, and feared more than they want to be loved. Charming right up until they aren't.
oldText.drive: To be, finally and undeniably, the name the frontier fears most — and to make Zuzu say it.
oldText.backstory: Every territory needs a deadliest, and the Magpie has spent a career furious that the title belongs to a quiet koala who doesn't even seem to want it. A thief turned killer turned legend-in-their-own-mind, they collect the shiny reputations of the people they've bested — and Zuzu's is the only one they've never managed to take.
oldText.presentation: A sleek black-and-white magpie in a dandy's waistcoat, every button and buckle a stolen trophy, grinning over a pair of polished pistols.
oldText.quirks: Steals one small shiny thing from every contract. Narrates their own legend aloud. Cannot resist a mirror.

mapping.label: The Stranger Who Posts the Bounties

oldText.name: The Stranger Who Posts the Bounties
oldText.personality: Haunted, methodical, and seeking a redemption that keeps receding. A monster trying to outrun its own reflection.
oldText.drive: To hunt down what they once were by proxy, one bounty at a time, until the ledger of old harm finally balances.
oldText.backstory: Every wanted poster in three territories is signed with the same mark, and nobody has seen who nails them up. The one who hunts monsters because they used to be one — each poster a confession written in other people's names, a way of atoning that has gotten badly out of hand.
oldText.presentation: A cloaked figure at a wanted-poster board under a desert moon, hammer in hand, a monstrous silhouette under the human shape.
oldText.quirks: Nails posters up at midnight. Signs with a mark, never a name. Hunts the crimes that mirror their own past.
oldText.artPrompt: A cloaked figure at a wanted-poster board under a desert moon, hammer in hand, a monstrous silhouette beneath the human shape, supernatural west, adult animated cartoon style, warm sepia and cold moonlight, crisp clean linework, simple background, no text

oldText.name: The Town That Walks
oldText.personality: Lumbering, protective, and surprisingly homey. A community that became a creature and never stopped caring for its own.
oldText.drive: To find a valley worth setting down in for good, and to keep every resident safe inside it until then.
oldText.backstory: It started as an ordinary frontier town and somewhere in a hard winter it decided to leave — pulled up its own foundations, grew great groaning legs of timber and stone, and walked off looking for better ground. The hundred souls who live in it came along, mostly because it asked nicely. The Town has a mayor, but the Town is also, increasingly, a citizen with a vote and a kindness toward the people in its streets.
oldText.presentation: A whole frontier town hoisted on enormous timber-and-stone legs striding across a dusty plain, lamplit windows glowing, a bell tower swaying.
oldText.quirks: Rearranges its own buildings to put people near friends. Steps carefully over wildlife. Rings its own bell when content.
oldText.artPrompt: A whole frontier town hoisted on enormous timber-and-stone legs striding across a dusty plain, lamplit windows glowing, bell tower swaying, supernatural west, adult animated cartoon style, warm sepia and amber, crisp clean linework, simple background, no text

oldText.name: Tomoe of the Long Road
oldText.personality: Grave, dogged, and quietly breaking. Built her whole self around a single purpose and is discovering, mile by mile, that purposes are not the same as people. Brave in the shaking way.
oldText.drive: To learn the truth of the night her family died, even if the truth costs her the vengeance that has kept her walking.
oldText.backstory: She has hunted Zuzu across a thousand dusty miles to avenge a family she watched die. She carries her father's sword and a story she's certain of — until she sees the koala shield a child from a bandit's blade without breaking stride, and the certainty begins, terribly, to crack.
oldText.presentation: A travel-worn young woman with a long braid and dust-grey road clothes, her father's katana held with white-knuckled care, eyes set on a horizon she's chased for years.
oldText.quirks: Sharpens her blade when she's thinking. Cannot tell a lie without her left hand betraying her. Counts her steps on long roads.

oldText.name: Zuzu
oldText.personality: Reserved and gravely polite; acts before speaking
oldText.drive: To finish the list he inherited without becoming the thing the list was made to stop.
oldText.backstory: A small, grave koala ronin whose silence and careful acts of mercy sit uneasily with his work as a hired sword.
oldText.presentation: short and stocky; slight paunch; rust-brown poncho with orange zigzag trim, dark tunic, orange sash, dark brown trousers, shallow wide-brimmed straw kasa; single sheathed katana diagonal across his back, hilt above right shoulder
oldText.quirks: Drinks eucalyptus tea before every contract. Never kills on an empty stomach. Keeps a tally that no one is allowed to see.

oldText.name: Zuzu's Last Name
oldText.personality: Patient, profound, and without judgment. The destination of a legend's whole journey. The question at the bottom of the list.
oldText.drive: To be reached, finally, by the one who has been riding toward it for years, and to witness which Zuzu arrives: the assassin the list demands, or the mercy he chose to become.
oldText.backstory: There is one name left on the list Zuzu inherited, and it has been waiting at the bottom for years. It is not a person. It is the reckoning itself, given a quiet shape — the last contract, the one that will either complete the oath or break it, the choice the whole long road was always walking toward. It sits at the end of every trail Zuzu rides, patient as a sunset, and it asks only one question, the same one it has asked since the beginning: when you reach me, will you be the blade the list made, or the mercy you've been bending it toward? It does not want an answer yet. It only wants the koala to arrive knowing the question is real.
oldText.presentation: A serene faceless figure of dusk-light seated at the end of a long western trail at sunset, a single unspoken name glowing softly where its heart would be.
oldText.quirks: Waits at the end of every trail. Asks the same question, gently, forever. Is a name, a reckoning, and a choice all at once.

oldText.title: Zuzu, Koala Assassin
oldText.description: You are Zuzu, the deadliest koala assassin the frontier has ever known, riding into a town with a secret worth killing for. Or play the young samurai who has hunted Zuzu across a thousand dusty miles to avenge a slaughtered family. Blades flash, loyalties shift, and only one of you is walking out of this town. Maybe neither.
oldText.inspirations: Yojimbo, Seven Samurai, Kung Fu Panda, Unforgiven, Lone Wolf and Cub
oldText.locations: Dusty Frontier Town, Samurai Village, The Hidden Canyon, Duel at Sunset

oldText.title: Mythic Frontier
oldText.description: You're a bounty hunter with a dead partner and a live problem: the warrant in your pocket is for a dragon, and the reward's been posted by the dragon itself. Out here the myths don't haunt the frontier—they run it, and they've decided you're useful. Every legend in Dragon Bone Canyon wants something, and none of them tell you the price until after you've agreed.
oldText.inspirations: Red Dead Redemption, American Gods, Deadlands, The Dark Tower, Unforgiven
oldText.locations: The Ghostly Saloon of Forgotten Heroes, Dragon Bone Canyon, The Griffin Roost Gold Mine, The Frontier Town Frozen in Myth

oldText.title: The Stranger Who Posts the Bounties
oldText.description: Every wanted poster in three territories is signed with the same mark, and nobody has ever seen who nails them up. Today you wait by the board at midnight to meet them. Whoever you choose to find gets generated as a character.
oldText.locations: The Bounty Board, Midnight Main Street, The Dust

oldText.title: The Eucalyptus Standoff
oldText.description: Zuzu the koala assassin has tracked the last name on a very old list to a tree-top teahouse at the edge of the territory. The target is waiting. They've been waiting a long time. They poured two cups.
oldText.genres: weird western, samurai standoff, marsupial menace
oldText.inspirations: Koala Assassin, the last name on the list
oldText.locations: The Tree-Top Teahouse, The Eucalyptus Canopy, The Edge of the Territory

oldText.title: Wanted, Dead or Stranger
oldText.description: The frontier's strangeness is best seen on its wanted posters. Four hang on the saloon wall tonight, each promising a bounty on something that shouldn't be bountiable. Pick one to render in full.
oldText.locations: The Saloon Wall, Moonlit Main Street, The Jailhouse Porch

oldText.title: The Crossroads Trading Post
oldText.description: Where four trails meet, a trading post run by a coyote in a duster deals in more than supplies. He lays four things on the counter, each leaving with you as something different.
oldText.genres: weird western, mercantile mystery, frontier magic
oldText.locations: The Crossroads Trading Post, The Four Trails, The Back Shelf

oldText.title: The Assassin's Quiet Hour
oldText.description: Between contracts, even the deadliest koala on the frontier needs a moment. Four glimpses of Zuzu off-duty. Pick one to render.

oldText.locations: The Lamplit Camp, The Eucalyptus Fork, The Contract Board, The Ridge

oldText.title: The Contract Broker's Back Room
oldText.description: Every assassin needs a fixer. Zuzu's broker — a tortoise who's outlived four generations of killers — slides four items across the table. Each leaves with you as something different.
oldText.inspirations: Koala Assassin, the broker's back room
oldText.locations: The Broker's Back Room, The Green Felt Table, The Territory Maps
